newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 to target women in ads.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 to target women in ads.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc. says it will target women -- who have been largely ignored by computer manufacturers -- in advertising campaigns for its personal computers and related products.
"I think you can expect to see our ads be a little less male and a little more diverse in terms of gender," Luanne Flikkema, Gateway's director of global research, said in an interview.
Flikkema recently carried out a study using Gateway surveys and focus groups and other research, which found women play a significant role in purchasing a personal computer for the home.

In an internal document dated September 1996, Gateway said the assumption of the PC industry, as reflected in its advertising, has been that the purchase of a computer was almost exclusively male-initiated and dominated.
In fact, Flikkema said women are more likely to control the family finances, making them an important sell.

"The biggest reason why women shouldn't be ignored is if Mom's head isn't nodding up and down, the PC doesn't get bought," she said. "If you can't convince her it's worth spending that money, there is not going to be a PC in the home."

A random survey of about 1,200 people, for example, found 47 percent of the time the male head of household played the major role in the purchase, 22 percent of the time it was the female and 28 percent of the time the purchase was handled equally by the male and female. Children drove purchases 3 percent of the time, Gateway found.
Gateway, which markets its PCs and equipment directly to buyers and not through retail stores, found women are less likely than men to consider buying computers directly.

"I think what we're facing here is an educational process -- remember 15 years ago people were saying women will never pick up the phone and buy something from a catalogue," Flikkema said, adding that women consider themselves less competent in the technology arena and prefer to see the machine and deal with a salesperson face-to-face.

"I think we're seeing that is going to change with PCs as well, as women get more and more comformatable with the technology and they realize what a time-saver and what a convenience it is to pick up the phone, order your PC and have it delivered right to your home," she said.
Flikkema said Gateway is promoting its customer service line, which is open all day everyday -- even Christmas Day. The company receives some 30,000 calls a day for sales and customer service.

In addition to including women in its ads, Gateway has begun television advertising, Flikkema said. In the internal report, it was recommended Gateway advertise in general interest and women's magazines and even sponsor women's sporting events.

"I think you're going to be seeing Gateway perhaps in more media than we've played in in the past," she said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see Gateway doing some media that is targeted toward women and kids."
